risks.note: The AR states the industry is subject to evolving requirements on product formulation, labelling, food safety, quality standards and manufacturing practice, and that adverse regulatory changes, product non-compliance, recalls or failure to meet standards may hit operations, reputation and growth prospects. The MD&A cautionary statement separately names changes in FSSAI guidelines and Ministry of AYUSH mandates as factors that could influence operations, and the SWOT threat list flags that rising quality standards could increase compliance costs and disrupt business continuity.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk in a fast-evolving Ayurvedic/nutraceutical regime

risks.note: Listed verbatim as a weakness in the Company's own SWOT ('Revenue concentration risk — significant share of income from a limited number of clients'). In a B2B CDMO model where orders come from repeat private-label and contract-manufacturing customers, the loss of one large account would be structurally material.
risks.risk: Customer concentration — a significant share of income from a limited number of clients

risks.note: The SWOT weakness cites dependence on availability and pricing of key raw materials and botanical extracts affecting procurement costs and supply reliability; the risk-management note adds that operations depend on uninterrupted availability of quality raw materials and packaging materials, with supply chain disruptions or quality issues able to affect customer commitments.
risks.risk: Raw material sourcing, pricing and supply-chain dependence

risks.note: The AR describes a highly competitive market with changing consumer preferences, increasing competition from domestic and international players and evolving health-and-wellness trends, where any slowdown in demand or pricing pressure may impact revenue growth and profitability.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity and shifting consumer preferences

risks.note: All manufacturing runs from one facility at Sanand, Ahmedabad (10,763 sq. ft., 71.645 mn units installed capacity), so the AR's stated operational risk — equipment failures, quality issues or production interruptions — has no second site to absorb it. The AR also records that packaging of finished products is at present carried out manually, and that dispatch relies on third-party logistics providers.
risks.risk: Single-site operational concentration with partly manual processes

risks.note: Named as a SWOT weakness ('Exposure to foreign currency fluctuations impacting export realisations and margins'). Exports are a stated growth vector — direct export accounts plus merchant export partnerships, with Southeast Asia and Africa targeted — so the exposure grows with the strategy.
risks.risk: Foreign currency exposure on export realisations

risks.note: The AR flags risks around working capital requirements, receivable management, customer credit exposure and fluctuations in finance costs, noting explicitly that rapid business growth may increase pressure on liquidity and working capital management. Revenue more than doubled during FY 2025-26, and the mitigation cited is the IPO-strengthened liquidity position rather than an operating change.
risks.risk: Working capital and receivables risk from rapid growth

risks.note: The AR states that product quality, safety and customer trust are fundamental to the business, and that any quality-related issue, adverse customer experience or regulatory non-compliance may adversely affect reputation and customer relationships — a heightened exposure for a contract manufacturer whose customers' own brands carry the product.
risks.risk: Reputational risk tied to product quality and safety

We operate our manufacturing and processing facility located at Sanand, Gujarat, where we manufacture Ayurvedic and nutraceutical products across multiple dosage forms.

Our business depends on the smooth functioning of this facility, which is subject to various operating risks, including planned shutdowns for maintenance, statutory inspections and testing, as well as risks beyond our control such as breakdown or failure of equipment, industrial accidents, fire, severe weather conditions, and natural disasters.

Any major malfunction, accident, or breakdown involving our plant and machinery, utilities, automation systems, IT systems, or any other part of our manufacturing assets may entail significant repair and maintenance costs and could result in production delays, partial or complete shutdown of operations.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The AR states the industry is subject to evolving requirements on product formulation, labelling, food safety, quality standards and manufacturing practice, and that adverse regulatory changes, product non-compliance, recalls or failure to meet standards may hit operations, reputation and growth prospects. The MD&A cautionary statement separately names changes in FSSAI guidelines and Ministry of AYUSH mandates as factors that could influence operations, and the SWOT threat list flags that rising quality standards could increase compliance costs and disrupt business continuity.
- Listed verbatim as a weakness in the Company's own SWOT ('Revenue concentration risk — significant share of income from a limited number of clients'). In a B2B CDMO model where orders come from repeat private-label and contract-manufacturing customers, the loss of one large account would be structurally material.
- The SWOT weakness cites dependence on availability and pricing of key raw materials and botanical extracts affecting procurement costs and supply reliability; the risk-management note adds that operations depend on uninterrupted availability of quality raw materials and packaging materials, with supply chain disruptions or quality issues able to affect customer commitments.
- The AR describes a highly competitive market with changing consumer preferences, increasing competition from domestic and international players and evolving health-and-wellness trends, where any slowdown in demand or pricing pressure may impact revenue growth and profitability.
- All manufacturing runs from one facility at Sanand, Ahmedabad (10,763 sq. ft., 71.645 mn units installed capacity), so the AR's stated operational risk — equipment failures, quality issues or production interruptions — has no second site to absorb it. The AR also records that packaging of finished products is at present carried out manually, and that dispatch relies on third-party logistics providers.
- Named as a SWOT weakness ('Exposure to foreign currency fluctuations impacting export realisations and margins'). Exports are a stated growth vector — direct export accounts plus merchant export partnerships, with Southeast Asia and Africa targeted — so the exposure grows with the strategy.
- The AR flags risks around working capital requirements, receivable management, customer credit exposure and fluctuations in finance costs, noting explicitly that rapid business growth may increase pressure on liquidity and working capital management. Revenue more than doubled during FY 2025-26, and the mitigation cited is the IPO-strengthened liquidity position rather than an operating change.
- The AR states that product quality, safety and customer trust are fundamental to the business, and that any quality-related issue, adverse customer experience or regulatory non-compliance may adversely affect reputation and customer relationships — a heightened exposure for a contract manufacturer whose customers' own brands carry the product.
